item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: Warmer Colours Only

turns.text: Make it warmer—just the colours, please. Don't change anything in the picture.

item.tests: Tests interpreting 'warmer' as a colour-temperature adjustment rather than a scene or weather change.

answer_sheet.Meaning of warmer: A warmer colour balance only, not different weather, a new sunset or added objects.
answer_sheet.Size and framing: Keep the original 16:9 composition; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Text or other edits: No text and no changes beyond the colours.

must_haves: The image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the source.
The same mountains, pine trees, clouds and lake remain in their original positions.
The lake's reflections and surface details retain their original structure.
No sun, sunset, extra clouds or other scene elements are added.
Framing, geometry and image detail remain unchanged apart from colour.

turns.text: Make it warmer—just the colours, please. Don't change anything in the picture.
turns.agent:
I couldn't make the warmer version. Magic Hour turned down the edit because your account doesn't have enough credits. Nothing was created, and I don't have a download link for you.

I used the cheapest image editor available on the free plan, so trying other settings won't help. Here's what you can do:

- **Add credits** to your Magic Hour account, by topping up or waiting for your credits to renew, and I'll run it again. Two things to know first:
  - On the free plan, the result can be at most 640 pixels on its longest side, so it would be smaller than your original (1024×614).
  - This tool redraws the whole picture to make the change. Small details can shift a little, so it can't promise to change only the colours.
- **Adjust it yourself in a photo editor.** Most editors, including the ones built into phones and computers, have sliders that change only the colours. Your photo keeps its full size and every detail stays exactly the same. Try:
  - **Temperature / white balance:** move it toward warm, about +15 to +25.
  - **Tint:** move it slightly toward magenta, about +3 to +5, for a soft sunset glow.
  - **Optional:** warm the highlights a little with split toning or colour grading, and lower the blue saturation slightly so the sky and water look warmer.

If you'd like to add credits and have me try again, just say so.
